transcript:
Header: 
Date: 2025-12-15
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Evan Martinez (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM); Liam O'Connor (Nova CTO), Sofia Reyes (ML Eng), Marcus Lin (Infra), Priyanka Rao (SecOps), Alex Kim (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): exploring migration path from OpenAI to Redwood Dedicated; discuss compatibility with vLLM/TGI stacks, model eval parity, security controls, and pilot scope.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Evan M: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Evan from Redwood, AE on the account, with Priya our solutions engineer, Jordan from CSM. Quick around-the-room?
[00:08] Liam O: Liam here, CTO. We've been running most inference on OpenAI, looking at dedicated options to reduce cost and gain more control over data residency.
[00:16] Sofia: Hi, Sofia — ML eng, I run the model evals and perf tests.
[00:21] Marcus: Marcus, infra, I handle VPCs and network.
[00:24] Priyanka: Priyanka, security, I'll be leading SOC2/compliance questions.
[00:29] Evan M: Great, thanks. Quick agenda: 1) understand current stack and pain points, 2) compatibility/interop questions (vLLM/TGI), 3) security and deployment options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), 4) next steps / pilot. Sound good?
[00:40] Alex: Yep that's good.

[02:05] Priya S: Can you talk a bit about your current flow — are you using raw OpenAI API calls or do you have a shim layer like vLLM or TGI?
[02:12] Sofia: Currently we call OpenAI for chat completions, but for bulk reranking and embedding workloads we've been experimenting with v L L M (vLLM) locally — it's a bit spotty. Some of our internal tooling uses T G I wrappers.
[02:27] Priya S: Got it. So compatibility with both the API surface and the model artifacts is important. Redwood's Hosted API is wire-compatible for most use cases, and Dedicated can run the same model variants we surface in the catalog. There are a couple notes about kv cache handling and streaming differences when you move to an on-prem/DEDicated runtime.
[02:45] Marcus: When you say 'kv cache handling' what exactly breaks? Our infra is sensitive to persistent state across pods.
[02:53] Priya S: Right — the runtime uses KV cache for generation acceleration. In a Dedicated setup it's handled within instance groups and isn't persisted beyond the inference job unless you configure persistent cache. If you have stateful routing we can discuss pinned sessions.

[04:10] Evan M: One thing we often see — eval parity: customers worry outputs will change when moving from OpenAI to an open model or a quantized variant. How much of that is a blocker for you?
[04:24] Sofia: It's big. We have guardrail tests that expect certain logits/behaviour. If we see regression we need a rollback plan.
[04:30] Priya S: We typically run side-by-side evaluations with a fixed prompt set. Redwood's Optimize tooling can snapshot outputs and flag regressions. For Dedicated, we can pin model versions and also provide recommended quant profiles — e.g., 4-bit quantization might introduce small diffs.
[04:50] Liam O: What's the fastest path to get parity? We don't want to re-tune hundreds of prompts.
[04:58] Priya S: Best practice is to start with full-precision variants and use our eval harness. If cost is a concern later, we can try INT8/4-bit quant with a candidate subset of prompts to validate. We can help run that bench.

[06:15] Marcus: On the infra front, we need to know network egress, IP whitelisting, and VPC peering options. Can Dedicated be deployed in our VPC?
[06:23] Evan M: Yes, Redwood Dedicated supports customer VPC peering for private networking. For fully air-gapped needs we offer Redwood Private with an on-prem package. We'll share the network diagram.

[08:00] Priyanka: Security questions — encryption at rest, KMS integration, and audit logs. We need SOC2 plus fine-grained RBAC and SSO/SAML integration.
[08:12] Jordan L: We have SOC 2 Type II, support for customer-managed KMS, detailed audit logs, and enterprise SSO (SAML/Okta). I'll attach the security pack after the call.
[08:25] Priyanka: Are logs accessible for long retention windows?
[08:30] Jordan L: Yes, log retention is configurable as an add-on.

[10:01] Sofia: A technical detail — we run TGI-based local stacks for faster local dev. Will Redwood Dedicated accept model artifacts exported from vLLM/TGI?
[10:13] Priya S: Usually yes; we support common model formats. There are occasional tokenizer mismatches and special ops where kernel selection differs. We recommend running a short import test and an eval pass.
[10:29] Sofia: Tokenizer mismatches have bitten us before.
[10:31] Priya S: We can assist there, and provide a tokenizer sanity check.

[12:05] Evan M: Cost modeling — how should you think about latency vs cost for rerank vs chat workloads?
[12:12] Marcus: We have low latency needs for chat (p95 < 200ms) and higher throughput for batch rerank.
[12:18] Priya S: Dedicated is ideal for predictable throughput and lower per-token cost at scale. Hosted gives fastest time-to-value but is more variable cost-wise. For very low latency you can tune instance types and batching parameters; we can run perf tests to meet your 200ms SLO.

[14:50] Liam O: If we move to Dedicated, what's the SLA and failover story?
[14:56] Evan M: Dedicated comes with an SLA; we also offer multi-zone placement and automated fallback to hosted variants if capacity issues arise. That said, fallback can change model variant — we'll define rollback semantics in the SOW.

[17:20] Sofia: Regarding eval parity again — can we do a blind A/B tests between OpenAI and the Redwood-hosted model without leaking prompts?
[17:28] Priya S: Yes, we can set up blind evals; best practice is to mask any PII and use hashed ids. We'll run the bench in a way that keeps your prompts private.

[19:00] Marcus: Are there quotas or limits we should be aware of during the pilot?
[19:07] Evan M: For Dedicated pilots we usually provision a known capacity window; we'll set a burst policy and alerts. No hidden throttles beyond configured quotas.

[21:40] Sophia (sic typo): (laughter) I keep typing Sophia vs Sofia — small thing.

[22:10] Evan M: Next, timelines: if you sign off on a pilot this month we can run a 4-6 week POC starting week of 12/22. Typical flow: baseline evals -> import/export checks -> perf bench -> small production shadowing.
[22:28] Liam O: That timeline works; our engineering bandwidth is limited over holiday but we can prioritize sample prompts.

[24:00] Priya S: For the benchmark we'll need: sample prompt set, typical request size distribution, target SLOs (latency/throughput), and any PII notes. Marcus, does infra have a preferred way to provide access?
[24:12] Marcus: We'll likely create a bastion host and limited egress rules. I'll send network peering details.

[26:30] Priyanka: A quick question on encryption — do you support customer-managed KMS for both Hosted and Dedicated?
[26:36] Jordan L: Customer-managed KMS is supported for Dedicated and Private; Hosted has options for customer keys in some enterprise tiers. We'll include specifics in the security pack.

[29:00] Sofia: Are there any gotchas when moving from deterministic OpenAI outputs to quantized open models?
[29:08] Priya S: Quantization can alter floating point behavior and sampling slightly; seeding and temperature adjustments sometimes compensate. Again, start with FP16/32 and validate.

[31:12] Evan M: Pricing preview — Dedicated is reserved capacity; we can show you a cost model based on your token volume and expected concurrency. We'll send an initial estimate.

[33:45] Sofia: Would Redwood run the initial bench or do we run it and share results?
[33:51] Priya S: We can run it together. Typically we run a Redwood-driven bench in your VPC or on a peered network to remove variability. We'll coordinate creds and sampling windows.

[36:05] Marcus: Integration with our CI/CD — can model rollouts be automated?
[36:11] Priya S: Yes, Redwood supports rollouts, canary deploys, and model pinning via APIs. You can trigger rollouts from CI to promote a model version. We'll share API docs.

[38:40] Liam O: Any regulatory considerations for data residency? We operate in EU and US.
[38:48] Evan M: We have region options, and Dedicated can be provisioned in specific regions for data residency. Private on-prem is available for strict regs. We'll map that in the SOW.

[41:00] Priya S: On the compatibility front — if you rely on TGI-specific runtime flags, we may need to map them to Redwood runtime flags; sometimes the behavior differs.
[41:10] Sofia: Noted. We'll surface the list.

[43:30] Evan M: Quick recap of agreed actions: we'll send pricing and SOW, security pack, and propose benchmark dates. Nova will send prompts, traffic profile, and infra contact.
[43:46] Liam O: Sounds good.

[45:00] Jordan L: I'll put the security docs link in the follow-up and include contact for SOC2 questions.
[45:08] Priyanka: Thanks everyone.
[45:12] Evan M: Thanks — we'll follow up with next steps by Wednesday.
[45:18] Sofia: Thanks, bye.
[45:20] Marcus: Bye.

[47:30] Call ended.

Notes: Transcript contains minor auto-transcription errors (speaker mislabels, 'v L L M' vs vLLM, 'S O' vs SSO, 'Sophia' typo). References to docs: deck & benchmarks spreadsheet shared via links above.
